passage: Some linguists argue that languages spoken in high mountain regions are more likely to include ejective consonants, sounds made with a burst of air from the throat, perhaps because they are easier to produce where air pressure is low. <u>Critics point out that many mountain languages lack ejectives, and that the pattern may reflect a few large language families rather than altitude itself.</u> The debate illustrates how hard it is to separate environmental influences on language from the effects of shared history.
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
choices: It presents an objection that the final sentence treats as an example of a broader difficulty.
It offers additional evidence supporting the idea that low air pressure at high altitude makes ejectives easier to produce.
It describes how ejective consonants are produced by speakers in mountain regions.
It explains why linguists first became interested in mountain languages.
steps: The underlined sentence gives critics' objections, including shared history as an alternative.
The final sentence generalizes: separating environment from shared history is hard.
So the sentence is an objection that illustrates the broader point, not support or description.
